records.title: Component Transfer Can Exceed Full Model Performance: Investigating Post-Trained Mixture-of-Experts
records.reason: The ACL paper studies transfer of attention, expert, and router components between post-trained MoE models to improve task performance; its abstract does not propose or measure inference-efficiency methods.

records.title: CAT: Circular-Convolutional Attention for Sub-Quadratic Transformers
records.reason: CAT replaces quadratic Transformer attention with circular-convolutional attention of O(N log N) complexity and reports lower runtime; this is a transferable sequence-computation optimization.

records.title: QIGen: Generating Efficient Kernels for Quantized Inference on Large Language Models
records.reason: QIGen automatically generates efficient kernels for quantized LLM inference on commodity CPUs and uses a hardware-aware performance model; this directly targets quantized inference execution.

records.title: Accelerating Vision Transformers Based on Heterogeneous Attention Patterns
records.reason: The paper exploits heterogeneous attention patterns to accelerate Vision Transformers through an integrated compression pipeline and reports up to 121% runtime-throughput improvement; the attention/compression method is transferable beyond vision.

records.title: Revisiting Offline Compression: Going Beyond Factorization-based Methods for Transformer Language Models
records.reason: The paper revisits offline compression for Transformer language models beyond factorization and explicitly targets memory-constrained deployment; it provides a direct model-compression method.

records.title: Sequence length scaling in vision transformers for scientific images on frontier
records.reason: The work studies sequence-length scaling for scientific-image Vision Transformers on frontier-scale hardware, emphasizing distributed training and sequence parallelism; this is a transferable systems technique, but the abstract does not establish LLM inference gains.

records.title: Flash normalization: fast RMSNorm for LLMs
records.reason: FlashNorm fuses or eliminates normalization work in Transformer inference, addressing a normalization bottleneck; the official arXiv abstract reports lower LLM latency, including Llama-7B results.

records.title: With Greater Text Comes Greater Necessity: Inference-Time Training Helps Long Text Generation
records.reason: Temp-LoRA stores long-context information in temporary low-rank adapters instead of retaining the full KV cache; the abstract reports lower memory and latency for long-text generation.

records.title: Scaling In-Context Demonstrations with Structured Attention
records.reason: Structured Attention removes dependencies between in-context demonstrations and reports up to 3.4× faster inference while scaling to hundreds of demonstrations; this is a direct attention/inference optimization.

records.title: FuxiMT: Sparsifying Large Language Models for Chinese-Centric Multilingual Machine Translation
records.reason: FuxiMT sparsifies large language models for Chinese-centric translation; its primary abstract describes structured sparsification to reduce computation while retaining translation performance, a transferable LLM-efficiency method.

records.title: Bird-Eye Transformers for Text Generation Models
records.reason: Bird-Eye Transformers adapts attention for text-generation quality and long-range context; the abstract provides no concrete reduction in inference compute, memory, or serving cost.

records.title: SparseCoder: Advancing source code analysis with sparse attention and learned token pruning
records.reason: SparseCoder combines sparse attention and learned token pruning for code analysis; the abstract reports faster execution and fewer inference FLOPs, a transferable sequence-sparsity technique.

records.title: How to Parameterize Asymmetric Quantization Ranges for Quantization-Aware Training
records.reason: The paper studies parameterizing asymmetric ranges for quantization-aware training and reports quantization-stability effects; its abstract is training-focused and does not show an inference-kernel or serving optimization.

records.title: Mamba Models a possible replacement for Transformers?
records.reason: The SciPy proceedings abstract compares Mamba with Transformer models for scientific computing and discusses efficiency tradeoffs, but does not establish a generally applicable LLM inference method or quantified serving optimization.

records.title: Exploring the Practicality of Generative Retrieval on Dynamic Corpora
records.reason: Generative retrieval for dynamic corpora uses a language model to retrieve documents and reports lower inference FLOPs, faster indexing, and lower storage than dual-encoder retrieval; it directly studies inference efficiency.

records.title: Self-Aligned Reward: Towards Effective and Efficient Reasoners
records.reason: Self-Aligned Reward targets efficient reasoning and reports that concise reasoning can reduce inference cost while retaining reward quality; the abstract makes the efficiency connection explicit.

records.title: Investigating the Effectiveness of HyperTuning via Gisting
records.reason: HyperTuning via Gisting compresses few-shot demonstrations into compact learned representations, but the abstract reports mixed task outcomes and does not quantify inference latency or serving-memory savings.

records.title: Legal-HNet: Mixing Legal Long-Context Tokens with Hartley Transform
records.reason: Legal-HNet mixes long-context legal tokens with Hartley-transform token mixing and reduces attention-related computation in its task setting; the abstract does not establish deployment gains outside its legal-domain model.

records.title: Does Acceleration Cause Hidden Instability in Vision Language Models? Uncovering Instance-Level Divergence Through a Large-Scale Empirical Study
records.reason: The title is a large empirical study of hidden instability in vision-language models, a robustness/reliability analysis rather than inference-efficiency work.

records.title: Defending MoE LLMs against Harmful Fine-Tuning via Safety Routing Alignment
records.reason: The title concerns defending MoE LLMs against harmful fine-tuning through safety alignment, a safety-training task rather than inference systems.
